citations.title: Georges Elhedery

sentences.text: Georges Bahjat Elhedery has been Group Chief Executive of HSBC Holdings plc since 2 September 2024, succeeding Noel Quinn.

sentences.quote: He most recently served as Group CFO between January 2023 and September 2024. Georges joined HSBC in 2005 with extensive trading experience in London, Paris and Tokyo.
sentences.text: He joined the bank in 2005 with trading experience in London, Paris and Tokyo, and served as Group Chief Financial Officer between January 2023 and September 2024, having been appointed to the board on 1 January 2023.

Earlier roles included Head of Global Banking and Markets for the Middle East and North Africa, Chief Executive for HSBC Middle East, North Africa and Turkiye, Global Head of Markets, and Co-Chief Executive of Global Banking and Markets.
He holds an engineering degree from the Ecole Polytechnique in Paris and a postgraduate degree in statistics and economics from ENSAE.
Born around 1974 in Beirut, Lebanon, he was named Euromoney's Banker of the Year in 2026.

sentences.text: Since taking over in September 2024, Georges Elhedery has executed a fast restructuring, replacing a complex matrix of three business lines and five regions with four units: corporate and institutional banking, international wealth and premier banking, Hong Kong and the UK, targeting $1.5bn of annualised cost savings by end-2026.

sentences.quote: reduce managing director positions by 15% under Elhedery, cutting global staffing costs by 8%. The restructuring also led to a reduced executive committee from 18 to 12 members
sentences.text: Managing director roles were cut 15% and the executive committee shrank from 18 to 12.
First-half 2026 return on tangible equity was 19.1% with CET1 at 14.1%, and buybacks resumed with up to $1bn after a three-quarter pause to rebuild capital following the Hang Seng Bank privatisation.
